clue.text: Lawyers talk of high winds in shelter

indicators.note: the strong winds are placed within the word for shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
gales are high winds

explanation.surface: Someone describes storm winds while sheltering, but it reads like a complaint about legal jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: The dense jargon used by lawyers in documents is called legalese, the language of the profession.

clue.text: Where soldiers may be caught leaving special units

indicators.note: the letter for caught departs from the soldiers' lodging word

parts.note: soldiers may be billeted in camps
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A picture of soldiers being caught leaving their special forces units.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperes are a particular kind of unit, those measuring electric current, hence special units.

clue.text: See 17
Large committee admitted to small reception

indicators.note: the large and committee letters are let into the word for small

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A large committee is squeezed into a small reception room.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome is the greeting or reception given to someone arriving.

clue.text: PM once almost overlooked parliamentary record, ignoring new religious school

indicators.note: the former prime minister's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Theresa May was a UK prime minister

indicators.note: read as looked over, i.e. read backwards, the shortened record is turned round
the letter for new is left out of the record's name

parts.note: Hansard is the official record of UK parliamentary debates

explanation.surface: A former prime minister supposedly missed the parliamentary record when opening a religious school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked' looks like the charade's verb, but read as 'looked over' it reverses the cut-down record; Hansard is the UK's printed transcript of parliamentary debates.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrasah is an Islamic college or school, so it is a religious place of learning.

clue.text: Guides graduate at new university in over complex points

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

indicators.note: the university letter sits within the jumbled letters
complex means intricate, so the letters of over and points are tangled

parts.note: E and S are two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A graduate at a new university guides others through complex points of argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guides' is a verb here, like the answer; 'points' means compass points, a standard crossword source of single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To manoeuvre something is to steer or guide it carefully, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Tricks won in clubs and hearts, without a king

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: the king's letter is taken out of the card suit's name

parts.note: taken as written, the suit name
R, for rex, is the Latin abbreviation for a king

explanation.surface: A card player's tricks won in clubs and hearts, though no king was held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes R (rex, king) from HEARTS to leave HEATS; 'won in' simply links the card-table surface to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat someone is to trick or swindle them, so tricks and cheats are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Infiltrate team prepared to stop father in France

indicators.note: the rearranged team plugs the middle of the French father, as a stopper fills a gap

parts.note: père is French for father

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters of team are reworked

explanation.surface: A team is trained to stop a French priest, an espionage plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' means to plug a gap, so the scrambled team fills the middle of the French father.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread through or penetrate something, much as an infiltrator gets into it.

clue.text: Helicopter swiftly circling hospital

indicators.note: the word for swiftly goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: apace means quickly or swiftly
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An air ambulance helicopter circles a hospital at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache is a well-known American attack helicopter made by Boeing.

clue.text: Trees with bark close to leaves

parts.note: to bay is to bark or howl, as hounds do

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the final letter of leaves is taken

explanation.surface: Trees with rough bark grow near their fallen leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay trees, the laurels whose leaves flavour cooking, are evergreen trees.

clue.text: Priestly pouch given to queen told off outside entrance to abbey

parts.note: a sac is a pouch or bag in an animal or plant
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the opening letter of abbey
off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of told are scrambled
the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A priest's pouch is handed to a queen, who scolds someone at the abbey door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TOLD to DOTL, and 'outside' wraps it round A, the first letter of abbey, giving DOTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacerdotal is a formal adjective relating to priests and the priesthood.

clue.text: Husband leaving shore working in lighthouse

indicators.note: the husband letter departs from the seaside word

parts.note: a beach is the shore
on means functioning or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A husband leaves the shore to go to work in a lighthouse, a keeper's life.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal light or fire, and a lighthouse is a coastal beacon.

clue.text: Rock star has cut of beef served with fruit

parts.note: chuck is a cut of beef from the shoulder
a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: A rock star at dinner has steak served with fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuck Berry was a pioneering American rock and roll guitarist and singer.

clue.text: Rodent in museum put down

parts.note: MUS is an abbreviation of museum
to quash a rebellion is to put it down

explanation.surface: A rodent found in a museum has to be put down.
explanation.definitionFit: A musquash is a muskrat, a large North American aquatic rodent.

clue.text: Composer's bottom rejected by topless minx

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for bottom is read backwards

parts.note: a bed is the bottom of a river or sea

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a minx is removed

parts.note: a hussy is a minx, a cheeky or brazen girl

explanation.surface: A composer's backside is spurned by a topless temptress.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Composer is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay; 'bottom' means a river bed, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was a French Impressionist who wrote music such as Clair de lune.

clue.text: Women into bags wanting large fabric samples

indicators.note: the women letter goes into the shortened bags
wanting means lacking, so the letter for large is left out

parts.note: satchels are bags

explanation.surface: Women stuff their bags with fabric samples, though not large ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' drops L from SATCHELS to give SATCHES; 'into' puts W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Swatches are small cut pieces of cloth shown as samples of a material.

clue.text: Ferryman carrying son nursed by old lovers to reach cult leader

indicators.note: the ferryman's name holds the other letters within it

parts.note: Charon is the ferryman of the dead in Greek myth

indicators.note: the son letter is held inside the lovers word, as a child is nursed

parts.note: leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A mythic boatman carries a son cared for by former lovers to reach a cult's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans two lights: this one and 3 down. Leman is an archaic word for a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Manson led the murderous 'Family' cult in late-1960s California.

clue.text: Attractive husband leaving awfully nice thing

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of nice thing are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An attractive husband walks out on something terribly nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' means the husband's H is taken from the pool: NICE THING without H, rearranged by 'awfully', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enticing tempts or lures you, so it is alluring and attractive.

clue.text: Put off by fuss about Japan's capital vessel

indicators.note: the fuss word goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother

indicators.note: a capital letter is the initial one, so the first letter of Japan is taken

parts.note: an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: Japan's capital puts off a ceremony over a fuss about a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to postpone or break it off until later.

clue.text: Boat on cart returned to recycling facility?

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing boat

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for cart is read backwards

parts.note: a dray is a cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A boat and a cart are taken back to the dump for recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapyard where discarded goods are salvaged and reused is a sort of recycling centre, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Universal lines taken from Shaping Trees written by Thomas More

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal

indicators.note: the letters for lines are removed from the gardening word

parts.note: topiary is the art of clipping trees and shrubs into shapes
RY, for railway, is an abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: A book title about tree shaping, with lines lifted from Thomas More.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' removes RY from TOPIARY to leave TOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is Thomas More's 1516 work describing an ideal island society.

clue.text: Money once made from fake tapes about Spain

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the Spain letter
fake means not genuine, so the letters of tapes are counterfeit, rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone made money long ago by selling counterfeit tapes about Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' rearranges TAPES into PESTA, and 'about' wraps that round E.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spain's currency before the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Shepherd almost over hill

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for over is dropped

parts.note: past means over or finished, as in the danger is past
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A shepherd is nearly over the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister who looks after a flock, a church shepherd by Christian metaphor.

clue.text: Find cameo carved on crucifix

indicators.note: carved means cut into a new shape, so the letters of cameo are reshaped

parts.note: a crucifix is a cross bearing Christ's figure

explanation.surface: A collector finds a cameo carved on a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across something is to find it by chance, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Streep finally gets to play Bond!

indicators.note: the final letter of the actress's name is taken

parts.note: to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: Meryl Streep at last gets to play James Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is an agreement that binds the parties, so it is a bond between them.

clue.text: Fastidious setter's following promising leads

indicators.note: following says the setter's word comes after the leading letters, not before
the leading letters of promising are taken from the front

parts.note: the setter is me, so setter's is I'm, I am

explanation.surface: A fussy setter follows promising leads.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves in clues, so setter's is I'M. 'leads' takes the two opening letters of promising here, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim describes someone stiffly proper and fussy, a synonym of fastidious.

clue.text: Wild fire damaged church

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters of fire are knocked out of shape

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wild fire has damaged a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce means savage or violent, as a wild animal is.

clue.text: Iron tree uprooted and set in a different position

indicators.note: uprooted means pulled out and displaced, so the letters of iron tree are rearranged

explanation.surface: An iron tree is uprooted and replanted somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorient something is to turn it to face a new direction or adjust its alignment.
